+# Cover archival
 
-As of 2022-11 there are 5,692,598 unarchived covers on ol-covers0 and archival hasn't occurred since 2014-11-29. This 5.7M number is sufficiently large that running `/openlibrary/openlibrary/coverstore/archive.py` `archive()` is still hanging after 5 minutes when trying to query for all unarchived covers.
+Cover IDs use exactly ten decimal digits. The first four digits identify a one-million-cover Internet Archive item; the next two identify a 10,000-cover ZIP batch. For example, cover `8819999` becomes `0008819999`, item `0008`, batch `81`.
 
-As a result, it is recommended to adjust the cover query for unarchived items within archive.py to batch using some limit e.g. 1000. Also note that an initial `id` is specified (which is the last known successfully archived ID in `2014-11-29`):
+Each cover has four variants: original (`''`), small (`s`), medium (`m`), and large (`l`). For each variant, the item is `<size_prefix>covers_<item_id>` and its ZIP is stored at `items/<size_prefix>covers_<item_id>/<size_prefix>covers_<item_id>_<batch_id>.zip` beneath `config.data_root`. The size prefix is empty for the original and `s_`, `m_`, or `l_` otherwise. Members are named `<10-digit-cover-id>.jpg`, `<10-digit-cover-id>-S.jpg`, `-M.jpg`, or `-L.jpg`. ZIP members are uncompressed for direct access through `https://archive.org/download/<item>/<zip>/<member>`.

+`archive.archive(test=False)` stages one 10,000-ID range at a time. It verifies the four local images, writes the ZIPs, then sets `archived=true`. During staging, `filename*` still point to the local images and `uploaded=false`. Missing local images are marked `failed=true`. The default `test=True` checks a range without writing ZIPs or changing records.
 
-# How to run Covers Archival
+Once a batch has been staged, run `Batch(item_id, batch_id).process_pending(upload=True, finalize=True)`. This uploads available ZIPs using `ia upload`, checks each ZIP with `ia list`, validates the ZIP contents and four matching cover sets, then atomically changes the batch's non-failed archived records to archive.org URLs and sets `uploaded=true`. A failed check leaves the records pointing to local images for a safe retry. Local images remain available until an operator separately cleans them up. A lock file next to each original-size ZIP serializes staging and upload/finalization of the same batch across processes sharing the data directory. Staging refuses a batch once any cover in its range is uploaded; finish adding covers to a range before finalizing it.

-# How it works
-
-As of 2022-11, the way coverstore works is that new covers that are uploaded to Open Library go into `/1/var/lib/openlibrary/coverstore/localdisk/` within a directory named `/YYYY/MM/DD/`. A record for each cover (and its size variants) is recorded within the `cover` table of the `coverstore` psql db located on `ol-db1`.
-
-At some (presumably advantageous if) regular interval, as the `localdisk` fills, the files can undergo archival, a process whereby covers are compressed and bundled into tar archives which are moved into the `/1/var/lib/openlibrary/coverstore/items/` directory within folders called "staging items" (e.g. `covers_0007`). The database reference to these covers' filename paths are updated accordingly by the `archive.py` script.
-
-Mek speculates that when coverstore attempts to look up a cover, its entry is looked up in the DB and if the filename is a tar, coverstore first looks on disk for a "staging item" folder within the staging directory `/1/var/lib/openlibrary/coverstore/items/` and if no such "staging item" exists, the staging item is assumed to have been uploaded as an archive.org item having the same name (and thus redirects/resolves its request via archive.org).  
-
-# State of Cover Archival
-
-As of 2022-11 there are 5,692,598 unarchived covers on `ol-covers0` and we're starting to run short on space. Specifically, cover archives haven't been happening since ~2014-11-29, as we can see from the following brutally slow query:
-
-```
-coverstore=# select id, olid, filename, last_modified from cover where archived=true order by id desc limit 1;
-
-   id    |    olid     |               filename               |       last_modified  
----------+-------------+--------------------------------------+----------------------------
- 7315539 | OL25645665M | covers_0007_31.tar:1849729536:247493 | 2014-11-29 22:34:37.329315
-```
-
-In the previous query, we see that the last cover (id #7,315,539) was archived on `2014-11-29` and resides within a tar `covers_0007_31.tar`. Coverstore assumes this tar resolves to an `item` folder called `covers_0007`, either staged on disk within `/1/var/lib/openlibrary/coverstore/items/` or on archive.org/details/covers_0007. In this case, at the time of writing, this item was still staged on disk. As far as Mek can tell, staged items presumably get manually uploaded to archive.org under an item having the same name.
-
-The item name itself (e.g. `coverd_0007`) is a combination of the prefix `covers` and the code `web.numify("%010d.jpg" % cover.id)[:4]` where, in this case, `cover.id` is `7315539`. The `"%010d"` format parameter pads the `cover.id` with leading 0's until it is 10 digits long and then the [:4] takes the first 4 digits of this padded number. Anything lower than `cover.id` 1,000,000 will thus be in `covers_0000` and from there the next 1M will be in `covers_0002` and so on. In total, this scheme allows for just under 10B covers before it breaks, which is a sufficiently unlikely number to hit!
-
-2022-12-03: Anand says: "The cover id is considered to be 10 digits, 4 digits go to items, 2 digits go to tar file and the remaining 4 go to the filename."

+import datetime
+import os
+import zipfile
+
+from openlibrary.coverstore import archive, config
+
+
+def test_cover_and_batch_paths(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(config, 'data_root', str(tmp_path))
+    assert archive.Cover.id_to_item_and_batch_id(8819999) == ('0008', '81')
+    assert archive.Batch(8, 81)._norm_ids() == ('0008', '81')
+    assert archive.Batch.get_relpath(8, 81, 's') == 'items/s_covers_0008/s_covers_0008_81.zip'
+    assert archive.Cover.get_cover_url(8819999, 's', protocol='http') == (
+        'http://archive.org/download/s_covers_0008/s_covers_0008_81.zip/0008819999-S.jpg'
+    )
+    assert archive.CoverDB._get_batch_end_id(8810000) == 8819999
+
+
+def test_zip_manager_deduplicates_and_stores_uncompressed(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(config, 'data_root', str(tmp_path))
+    source = tmp_path / 'source.jpg'
+    source.write_bytes(b'image')
+    manager = archive.ZipManager()
+    name = '0008819999-L.jpg'
+    timestamp = datetime.datetime(2020, 1, 1).timestamp()
+    manager.add_file(name, str(source), timestamp)
+    manager.add_file(name, str(source), timestamp)
+    manager.close()
+    path = archive.Batch.get_abspath(8, 81, 'l')
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as result:
+        assert result.namelist() == [name]
+        assert result.getinfo(name).compress_type == zipfile.ZIP_STORED
+        assert result.read(name) == b'image'
+    assert archive.count_files_in_zip(path) == 1
+
+
+def test_batch_only_finalizes_complete_uploaded_set(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(config, 'data_root', str(tmp_path))
+    class FakeUploader:
+        def __init__(self):
+            self.uploaded = set()
+        def is_uploaded(self, item, filename):
+            return (item, filename) in self.uploaded
+        def upload(self, item, filepaths):
+            self.uploaded.add((item, os.path.basename(filepaths[0])))
+
+    uploader = FakeUploader()
+    finalized = []
+    monkeypatch.setattr(archive.CoverDB, 'update_completed_batch', staticmethod(lambda *ids: finalized.append(ids)))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(archive.db, 'getdb', lambda: type('DB', (), {'select': lambda *args, **kwargs: []})())
+    batch = archive.Batch(8, 81)
+    assert not batch.process_pending(upload=True, finalize=True, uploader=uploader)
+    assert not finalized
+    for size in archive.SIZES:
+        path = archive.Batch.get_abspath(8, 81, size)
+        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(path, 'w') as z:
+            z.writestr(f'0008810000{"-" + size.upper() if size else ""}.jpg', b'image')
+    assert batch.process_pending(upload=True, finalize=True, uploader=uploader)
+    assert finalized == [('0008', '81')]
